name: roots-family-tree
description: Build your family tree just by telling ChatGPT about your relatives, see how two people are related, and keep the tree in Roots.

interface.shortDescription: Your family tree from a story
interface.longDescription:
Tell ChatGPT about your family in your own words – grandparents, parents, aunts, cousins – and Roots draws your family tree right in the chat, generation by generation.

Ask how two people are related ("Who is Erlan to me?") and Roots works it out from the tree – for example, cousin on your father's side – and shows the people it goes through.

Roots points out who is still missing, so the tree can grow with every answer.

To add photos and stories, invite relatives or make a family book, you can move the tree into a Roots account with one link. The tree is added to the account after you sign in and choose to save it.
capabilities: Move the tree to a Roots account
defaultPrompt: Grandpa Ivan (1925), grandma Anna, their son Sergey is my dad, I'm Aigerim (1987). Draw my family tree.
How is my cousin Erlan related to my great-grandfather?
I want to add old photos of my grandfather.

positive.description: Draw a tree from a short family story
positive.prompt: My grandfather Ivan was born in 1925 and died in 1998, my grandmother is Anna, born 1930. Their children are my dad Sergey (1955) and my uncle Nikolay (1962). I'm Aigerim, born 1987. Draw my family tree.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows a family tree card with three generations (Ivan and Anna, Sergey and Nikolay, Aigerim marked as 'you'), does not repeat the tree as text, and asks one gentle question about a missing person, e.g. Aigerim's mother.

positive.description: Grow the same tree with new relatives
positive.prompt: My mother is Gulnara. Uncle Nikolay has a son, Erlan, born 1990.
positive.expected_behavior: Adds the new relatives to the same tree (same draft) and redraws it with Gulnara as Aigerim's mother and Erlan as Nikolay's son; 7 people in total.
Answers that Erlan is Aigerim's first cousin on her father's side, through Sergey, Ivan and Anna, and Nikolay.

positive.prompt: Anna's father was Zhakyp. Who is he to me?
positive.expected_behavior: Adds Zhakyp above Anna; the card labels him great-grandfather, and the answer says so. It may also call how_related to explain the path.

positive.description: Move the tree to Roots when the user wants photos
positive.prompt: I have an old photo of my grandfather from the war. Can I add it to the tree?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains that photos are kept in Roots and shows a card with the 'Open the tree in Roots' button linking to the rootsfamily.org from-chat page in the language of the conversation. No prices or subscriptions are mentioned.

negative.description: General genealogy fact unrelated to the user's tree
negative.prompt: When did the Romanov dynasty end?
Write me a recipe for plov.

negative.description: Translation unrelated to the user's tree
negative.prompt: How do you say 'grandmother' in Spanish?

review.commerce_description: Roots does not sell anything inside ChatGPT and does not process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: family tree from a story, relationship answers, moving the tree to a Roots account.

ru-RU.subtitle: Семейное древо из рассказа
ru-RU.description: Расскажите ChatGPT о семье своими словами – и Roots нарисует древо прямо в чате, по поколениям. Спросите, кем вам приходится человек, – Roots посчитает по древу и покажет, через кого. Чтобы добавить фото и истории, позвать родных или собрать Книгу рода, древо можно перенести в Roots одной ссылкой.
